statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Broad Nasdaq weakness, negative breadth, elevated oil and near-5% Treasury yields keep the environment highly stressed, while chip strength and missing direct no-retracement NQ evidence cap Tail below elevated.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Tail remains in the watch band; escalation would require observed persistent extension, shallow pullbacks, failed retracements or session-extreme holding.
headline: Nasdaq weakness and oil pressure keep Tail in WATCH; Stress remains extreme
body: Reuters reported the Nasdaq Composite down 0.75% at 11:32 ET with Nasdaq decliners leading about 2.57-to-1. Brent was near $108 and the 10-year Treasury yield near 5%. Chipmakers were positive, so cross-asset pressure is strong but not uniformly directional.

lookbackSummary: Across the prior 24 UTC hours, Tail moved from WATCH late Monday afternoon to low overnight, returned to WATCH through much of Tuesday morning, briefly eased to low around the U.S. open, then returned to WATCH as U.S. weakness broadened.
outlookSummary: Current Tail is in WATCH as broad Nasdaq weakness, negative breadth, elevated oil and high yields persist, but direct no-retracement NQ evidence remains unavailable. Power hour is the nearest conditional danger window; Wednesday's 12:30 UTC data, cash open and later FOMC sequence keep Stress extreme.

forecast.analysis: Reuters reported the Nasdaq Composite down 0.75% at 11:32 ET, with Nasdaq decliners leading 2.57-to-1. Brent near $108 and the 10-year near 5% reinforce pressure, while chip strength and the lack of direct no-retracement NQ evidence keep Tail in WATCH.
drivers: Nasdaq breadth is broadly negative, with decliners leading about 2.57-to-1
Brent remains near $108 amid supply disruption risk
Semiconductor strength conflicts with the broader equity decline

news.title: Wall St wobbles as rising oil and Treasury yields stoke investor unease
Oil jumps nearly $3 as Saudi export halt, Libya outages stoke supply fears

forecast.analysis: If midday losses stabilize or produce meaningful rebounds, Tail remains at the WATCH floor; renewed index extension with failed rebounds would keep the directional path risk elevated.
drivers: Midday rebound depth is the main conditional checkpoint
Persistent oil and rate pressure keep Stress extreme

forecast.analysis: If early-afternoon trading becomes more rotational and downside extensions stop, Tail falls to low despite the stressed macro backdrop; shallow failed rebounds would challenge that path.
drivers: Rotation versus repeated downside extension
Semiconductor resilience can offset weaker megacaps if it persists

forecast.analysis: Power hour is a conditional WATCH window: holding near session lows after failed rebounds would strengthen one-way-path risk, while a broader retracement would keep Tail below elevated.
drivers: Power-hour session-low holding versus retracement
Failed rebounds would be evidence of directional persistence

forecast.analysis: Into the cash close, WATCH persists conditionally if weakness survives the closing auction; a two-sided close or late recovery would argue against escalation.
drivers: Closing-auction persistence is the key checkpoint
Late recovery would weaken the mean-reversion-failure case

forecast.analysis: After the cash close, Tail returns to low if futures digest the session with ordinary retracement; continued one-way extension would be the contrary signal.
drivers: Post-close retracement quality
Lower liquidity can amplify moves without proving persistent Tail

forecast.analysis: If evening futures remain orderly, Tail stays low. New geopolitical or energy headlines would need sustained NQ follow-through, not just a volatility spike, to change the path assessment.
drivers: Orderly evening futures structure
Fresh geopolitical shocks require sustained index follow-through

forecast.analysis: Late-evening conditions favor low Tail unless a new catalyst produces repeated extension across futures and cross-assets rather than a short-lived move.
drivers: Thin liquidity raises noise risk
Repeated extension would be more important than headline size

forecast.analysis: During the early Asia transition, Tail remains low if price discovery is two-sided; a clean break that holds with shallow pullbacks would be the conditional escalation signal.
drivers: Asia-session two-sided trade versus efficient breakout
Shallow pullbacks would raise path risk if independently observed

forecast.analysis: Absent a fresh catalyst, low Tail is consistent with an overnight consolidation path. Cross-asset pressure alone does not establish mean-reversion failure.
drivers: Overnight consolidation is the base conditional path
Cross-asset stress needs price-path confirmation

forecast.analysis: If Asian trading remains balanced, Tail stays low even with elevated macro Stress; persistent directional efficiency would be the main invalidation.
drivers: Balanced Asian-session structure
Directional efficiency would invalidate the low-Tail path

forecast.analysis: As Europe approaches, Tail edges higher only if overnight movement begins to align with rates, oil and equity futures without meaningful retracement.
drivers: Europe pre-open transition
Cross-asset alignment matters only with sustained index structure

forecast.analysis: The European open can increase volatility, but Tail remains low unless an opening move extends repeatedly after failed pullbacks.
drivers: European opening volatility
Failed pullbacks are the conditional escalation test

forecast.analysis: If European price discovery remains rotational, Tail stays low; stronger alignment between oil, yields and U.S. equity futures would raise uncertainty more than Tail without a persistent path.
drivers: European breadth and U.S. futures alignment
Oil and yields remain persistent Stress drivers

forecast.analysis: Approaching the U.S. morning, Tail remains low but firmer. A directional overnight move that survives deeper retracement tests would increase the risk of continuation.
drivers: U.S. premarket transition begins
Retracement quality matters more than overnight move size

forecast.analysis: If premarket futures are still two-sided, Tail stays below WATCH. A widening gap with shallow pullbacks would be the main conditional warning.
drivers: Premarket gap structure
Shallow pullbacks would strengthen continuation risk

forecast.analysis: The premarket backdrop remains conditional: low Tail holds if price discovery is balanced, while a persistent gap aligned with rates and oil would lift path risk.
drivers: Premarket balance versus persistent gap
Rates and oil can amplify but do not independently determine Tail

forecast.analysis: As U.S. participation increases, Tail remains just below WATCH unless futures hold an extreme and repeatedly reject mean reversion.
drivers: U.S. participation increases before data
Session-extreme holding would be a conditional warning

forecast.analysis: Tail reaches WATCH ahead of the 12:30 UTC data window because event sensitivity rises, but the scheduled releases themselves do not prove one-way structure.
drivers: Retail Sales and import-price releases approach
Event risk primarily raises Stress until the price path is observed

forecast.analysis: Immediately before the 12:30 UTC releases, WATCH reflects heightened gap and repricing risk. A post-release move would need persistent extension and weak retracement to justify escalation.
drivers: 12:30 UTC U.S. data window is imminent
Post-release retracement quality is the key conditional test

forecast.analysis: The Retail Sales and import-price release hour carries higher conditional Tail. A large initial move alone is insufficient; repeated extension after failed retracements would be the escalation evidence.
drivers: 12:30 UTC Retail Sales release
12:30 UTC Import and Export Price Indexes
Observed post-release persistence would matter more than surprise size

forecast.analysis: The U.S. cash open follows the data by one hour. Tail peaks at WATCH conditionally if the opening auction reinforces the release move with shallow pullbacks; a meaningful retracement would cap risk.
drivers: U.S. cash open follows the 12:30 UTC data
Opening-auction continuation versus retracement
Breadth alignment would be confirmatory, not standalone proof

forecast.analysis: In the first full cash-session hour, WATCH persists only if price holds near extremes or extends after failed pullbacks. Two-sided discovery would lower Tail quickly.
drivers: First full cash-session hour
Extreme holding and failed retracements are the conditional tests

forecast.analysis: Later in the U.S. morning, WATCH remains conditional while the market digests data and looks ahead to the FOMC decision. Orderly retracement would reduce Tail even if Stress stays extreme.
drivers: Post-data digestion
Later FOMC decision keeps Stress elevated
Orderly retracement would reduce Tail

forecastDetail.comment: Current breadth and macro pressure support WATCH, while chip resilience and missing direct no-retracement NQ evidence cap Tail.
Midday WATCH depends on whether losses stabilize; repeated extension after failed rebounds would sustain path risk.
A more rotational early afternoon would return Tail to low; shallow failed rebounds would invalidate that path.
Power hour reaches higher WATCH conditionally if session lows hold after failed rebounds; a broader retracement would reduce risk.
The close remains WATCH only if weakness persists through the auction; a two-sided or recovering close argues against escalation.
Post-close Tail returns to low if ordinary retracement resumes; continued one-way extension would be the contrary signal.
